Reference › Error codes

Error codes

Husk reports through MSBuild in a build and through the app's log in Development. Both print the same shape: file(line,col): error HUSK100: code: message, with Svelte's line and a 1-based column. A failed source gets no new output: the build fails and keeps the previous files, and the Development app keeps serving the last good ones.

Svelte's own codes (a11y_missing_attribute, expected_token) come after the Husk code; they are listed in Svelte's docs.

Code Kind Message
HUSK001 error (MSBuild) Husk cannot build on this platform
HUSK002 error (MSBuild) Husk needs Extrode.Pare.Build
HUSK003 error (MSBuild) V8's native library for this machine was not restored
HUSK004 error (MSBuild) another Husk version already started V8 in this build process
HUSK100 error Svelte could not compile the source
HUSK101 error the outputs the build gave do not match the source
HUSK102 error a file cannot be read or written
HUSK200 warning a Svelte compiler warning

HUSK001

The build machine is not one of the six V8 ships for: win-x64, win-arm64, osx-x64, osx-arm64, linux-x64 and linux-arm64 (glibc). A musl Linux (Alpine), FreeBSD and the like fail here, before anything compiles. Build on a supported machine; the output is plain JavaScript and CSS and runs anywhere.

HUSK002

The project references Extrode.Husk.Build but not Extrode.Pare.Build. NuGet imports a package's build targets only into projects that reference it directly, and Husk's build runs inside Pare's, so the project references both:

XML 
<PackageReference Include="Extrode.Pare.Build" Version="0.7.0" PrivateAssets="all" />

HUSK003

Extrode.Husk.Build carries no V8 library itself. It depends on Microsoft's Microsoft.ClearScript.V8.Native.<rid> packages at exactly 7.5.1.1, and the build looks for the one for this machine in the NuGet cache. The file is missing when the project was not restored, when a package source mapping does not allow Microsoft.ClearScript.*, or when the app pins another version of a Microsoft.ClearScript.V8.Native.* package (a lower pin is NU1605; a higher one means 7.5.1.1 is never downloaded). Restore the project, allow the packages, or remove the pin.

HUSK004

dotnet build keeps its build processes running for a few minutes and reuses them. One that has already compiled with one Extrode.Husk.Build version holds that version's V8; a second version cannot safely load its own copy beside it, so the build stops instead. It happens after upgrading Husk while those processes still run, or in a solution whose projects use different Husk versions. Run dotnet build-server shutdown and build again; in a solution, give every project the same version.

HUSK100

Svelte rejected the source; its code and message follow (expected_token, js_parse_error). In Development it is also logged when the compiler itself failed, with the exception. A .svelte.ts that Pare cannot strip is logged as HUSK100 with Pare's code as the message (PARE100 and up for syntax it cannot erase, PARE001 for a syntax error; see Pare's error codes). Search for the HUSK100 code, not PARE1xx.

HUSK101

The build gave a source outputs Husk does not write: a missing .svelte.css or .js.map item, or an output path that is the source itself (a .svelte.js outside wwwroot with no PareOutDir property; set the PareOutDir project property, or move it below wwwroot). In Development it means the app was built by an older Husk than the one compiling; rebuild.

HUSK102

A source, output, page, husk.css or importmap.json could not be read or written: the file is locked, the disk is full, or the folder is read-only. The message carries the operating system's reason. Outputs that failed are written again by the next build.

HUSK200

A Svelte compiler warning, such as a11y_missing_attribute for an <img> without alt. It does not fail the build; <TreatWarningsAsErrors> or <WarningsAsErrors>HUSK200</WarningsAsErrors> makes it. Then, as with HUSK100, that source's outputs are left as they were, so the next build fails on it again instead of finding it up to date.
